claims.statement: doc/Deep16-FPU.md is a 732-line FPU specification with a fixed two-register window (F0=R2:R3, F1=R4:R5) and IEEE-754 single precision, but no floating-point implementation exists in js/, rtl/ or the WASM source.
FPUEMUPLAN.md and FLOATIMPL.md are design notes that explicitly declare nothing implemented.

The ILL trap exists only in core3 and covers only DIV/DIV32: a division that needs the iterative divider (non-zero divisor, and for DIV32 an even destination) redirects to the vector at physical address 0 instead of executing.
The full D16 core keeps a hardware divider, so only the reduced core needs the ILL workaround.
The D16nano kernel installs a vector-0 ILL handler and emulates DIV and DIV32 in software.
There is no general undefined-opcode or FPU trap; only the DIV/DIV32 case is trapped, and an unknown word does not raise ILL.

The SIC wires only the timer tick: the source vector is {raster_src, 0, timer_tick, 0}, raster_src is guarded by the D16_NANO macro that no build defines, and the I2S fifo_irq output is left unconnected.
core3 accepts a level IRQ at an instruction boundary and enters the handler through the vector word at physical address 1, while the full deep16_core has no interrupt input.
The JS core implements handleHardwareInterrupt and an irqLine hook, and the WASM core has neither an interrupt input nor an interrupt handler.

README's statement that hardware-interrupt handling exists only in the JS core and that the RTL core has neither predates core3, which does implement interrupt entry; three-core interrupt behaviour still differs.
WASM lacks the SIC, SPI, SD and screen models, and has no interrupt input, while the JS core models SD/SPI/SIC and carries a d16nano ILL flag.

The short core-counter line is implemented for narrow screens: responsive CSS hides .core-stats and shows .core-stats-mini below 900 px, and the controller fills both with CPI and cache rate, while README still says the short form is not visible on phones.
js/deep16_worker.js is a complete simulator worker, but no Worker is constructed, no script tag loads it, and workerRun posts to an undefined this.worker, so execution stays on the main thread.
doc/ is the single current documentation set and old/ keeps superseded versions and Lua tooling as reference only.
MEMMAP.md claims CS1 is pin 25 and the on-board configuration flash is unused, while the tile build boots from that flash over MSPI pins 59-62 and pin 25 is I2S BCLK.
MEMMAP.md describes UART divisor 234 as the 27 MHz value, while the RTL derives the divisor from CLK_HZ divided by BAUD.
The WASM source comment claiming the RTL keyboard FIFO has 128 entries is stale; deep16_top uses a 16-entry FIFO.

The root plan documents each declare their own status: TODO open, SCROLLPLAN in progress, BIRDPLAN plan only, SLIMPLAN a measured design note, IMPROVE planned-not-applied, ERRPLAN open items, FROGPLAN a plan with a hardware update, FPUEMUPLAN agreed but unimplemented.

VERSIONING.md proposes three independently bumped component versions and a VERSION file feeding generated asm and RTL headers, but declares the scheme unimplemented and none of the named artifacts or generator exist.

book/README.md is a German draft plan titled 'Deep16 für 6502-Programmierer', organised into three parts and eight chapters plus appendices, and it ends with open questions on length and 6502 contrast.

STATUS.md is a 1,381-line German log for the book and Forth kernel, last changed 2026-10-16, whose known-defects section says none and whose open-work list covers the Forth tier-3 word set, browser source typing, chapters 9+, and unimplemented GFX.
lila/ is a host-side prototype compiled to Forth and run under gforth, supporting assignments, arithmetic, strings, conditionals, loops, break, functions and tables; it does not run on the Deep16.
README reports that the original project summary claimed PRODUCTION READY and explicitly calls that aspirational marketing text rather than a status report.

README's verified positive case is that all three cores agree, assembler and disassembler round trip, examples assemble and run, the Forth kernel is an interactive REPL on all three cores, and the RTL core is verified across the instruction space.
